accepted.quote: would provide an exemption to CFPB's funding cut to ensure they have sufficient funding to fully implement their Sec. 1033 rule to promote open banking and data privacy.
accepted.rationale: The amendment seeks to preserve funding to implement open banking and data privacy protections.

accepted.quote: would ensure CFPB has sufficient funding to ensure consumers are protected from unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices (UDAAP) related to Artificial Intelligence (AI)
accepted.rationale: The amendment seeks to maintain CFPB funding to protect consumers from AI-related abusive practices.

accepted.quote: would ensure CFPB has sufficient funding to operate the consumer complaint database and ensure financial firms respond to complaints.
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports continued operation of the consumer complaint database and firm responsiveness.

accepted.quote: would require an FSOC and OFR study on the financial stability impact of the use of social media and other unofficial channels, including those personally owned by the President, to convey major policy initiatives,
accepted.rationale: The amendment calls for study of financial stability risks from unofficial policy communications.

accepted.quote: would block the White House from undermining CFPB's independence by prohibiting its ability to review or modify CFPB's budget or proposed rules and guidance before it is finalized.
accepted.rationale: The amendment seeks to protect CFPB independence from White House interference.

accepted.quote: would strike Section 5001 and replace it with funding for the HOME and CDBG programs to build, rehabilitate, and preserve affordable and resilient housing
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports funding affordable housing programs to lower costs and aid recovery.

accepted.quote: would ensure CFPB has sufficient funding for the purpose of ensuring student borrowers are protected.
accepted.rationale: The amendment seeks to preserve CFPB funding to protect student borrowers.

accepted.quote: ensures that CFPB has sufficient funding for the purpose of implementing interpretative guidance on how payment consumer protections apply to emerging digital payment mechanisms, including those offered through video gaming platforms.
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports applying payment protections to emerging digital payment mechanisms.

accepted.quote: would prevent the CFPB rollbacks and funding cuts from taking effect unless Treasury certifies that fees and other financing costs will be reduced for every consumer financial product.
accepted.rationale: The amendment conditions CFPB cuts on certification that consumer costs will fall.

accepted.quote: would make the effective date of the PCAOB related section effective only upon certification by the SEC that retirement savers would not be exposed to greater risk,
accepted.rationale: The amendment seeks to protect retirement savers from risks of eliminating PCAOB inspections.

accepted.quote: would require the Fed to conduct a study on the impact tariffs have on the cost of goods and services for consumers.
accepted.rationale: The amendment calls for study of tariff impacts on consumer costs.

accepted.quote: would maintain CFPB's robust funding and replace their funding mechanism with industry assessments, including on megabanks, big tech payment providers, and payday lenders.
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports maintaining CFPB funding through industry assessments.

accepted.quote: would maintain CFPB's robust funding and replace their funding mechanism with assessments on financial firms that broke consumer financial protection laws.
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports sustaining CFPB funding via assessments on violators.

accepted.quote: would require FSOC and OFR to study DOGE cuts and their negative effect on consumer harm and financial stability.
accepted.rationale: The amendment calls for study of negative effects of DOGE cuts on stability.

accepted.quote: would require FSOC member agencies to report to Congress on the types and amounts of sensitive data that DOGE has had access to,
accepted.rationale: The amendment seeks reporting on DOGE access to sensitive data and related risks.

accepted.quote: allow FSOC to study the effects of Trump's ownership of a crypto company that is creating a stablecoin and crypto exchange,
accepted.rationale: The amendment calls for study of competition and stability risks from crypto ownership.

accepted.quote: authorizes the SEC $3.2 billion, to be offset by fees on well-known seasoned issuers (large public companies), to carry out the duties that PCAOB would now no longer do,
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports funding SEC to assume PCAOB auditor oversight duties.

accepted.quote: Strikes Sec. 50002, to not dismantle the PCAOB.
accepted.rationale: The amendment opposes dismantling the PCAOB audit oversight board.

accepted.quote: would allow FSOC to investigate the President and other government officials who are gaining financial benefit from their ownership and marketing of crypto products for conflicts of interest that may harm financial stability.
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports investigating crypto conflicts that may harm financial stability.

accepted.quote: would allow FSOC to monitor risks to financial stability arising from the government potentially requiring the use of particular stablecoins and other digital assets to contract with the government.
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports monitoring stability risks from mandated stablecoin use.

accepted.quote: would require an FSOC and OFR study on the impact that the President's attempt to undermine the independence of the Federal Reserve has on the economy, price stability, maximum employment, and dollar primacy.
accepted.rationale: The amendment calls for study of economic impacts from undermining Fed independence.

accepted.quote: would prevent these FSC provisions from taking effect if the government extends or expands tax cuts for wealthy individuals or large corporations.
accepted.rationale: The amendment opposes advancing provisions alongside tax cuts for wealthy and corporations.

accepted.quote: would prevent these FSC provisions from taking effect if the government cuts funding for Medicaid, Social Security, or Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).
accepted.rationale: The amendment opposes provisions if safety-net program funding is cut.

accepted.quote: would provide over $150 billion in robust new investment in housing to address the crisis.
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports large new investment to address the housing crisis.

accepted.quote: would provide full funding for 60,000 Emergency Housing Vouchers.
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports full funding for emergency housing vouchers.

accepted.quote: would strike Section 50001 and replace this section with funding to address the public housing capital backlog.
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports funding to address the public housing capital backlog.

accepted.quote: would strike Section 50001 and replace this section with Rep. Green's Reforming Disaster Recovery Act.
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports replacing the section with disaster recovery reform.

accepted.quote: Any remaining amounts in the fund that come from enforcement actions for violations of the Military Lending Act shall be transferred to the Department of Housing and Urban Development and the Department of Veteran Affairs HUD-VASH program.
accepted.rationale: The amendment supports directing Military Lending Act penalties to veteran housing.
